match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the distinction between autosomes and sex chromosomes, and homologous pairs and alleles on the X are only related: meiosis covers how chromosome pairs separate, and sex-linked inheritance covers X-linked traits, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Autosomes and sex chromosomes
card: Homologous chromosomes are a matching pair, one from each parent. They are the same length and carry the same genes in the same order, but they may carry different alleles.
all chromosomes that are not sex chromosomes. Humans have 22 pairs, and these pairs look the same in females and males.
the pair that differs between the sexes and helps decide whether a person is female or male. Humans have one pair, made of X and Y chromosomes.
A human female has two X chromosomes, which are homologous. A human male has one X and one Y. The X and Y are different sizes and carry mostly different genes, so they are not a true matching pair.
draft.remember: Homologous chromosomes carry the same genes. Autosomes look alike in both sexes, but the sex chromosomes can differ.

a.q: Which statement correctly describes a pair of homologous autosomes in a human?
opts: They carry the same genes, perhaps with different alleles
They carry the same genes and always identical alleles
They carry different genes, so each has its own role
They differ in size between females and males
a.why: Homologous chromosomes carry the same genes in the same order, but each one may carry a different allele of a gene. They do not always carry identical alleles, and autosomes look the same in females and males.
a.clue: Think about genes and alleles on a matching pair.

b.q: A karyotype of one human cell shows 22 matching pairs and a 23rd pair of chromosomes of clearly different sizes. What does this tell you about the person?
opts: The person is male, with an X and a Y chromosome
The person is female, with two X chromosomes
The person is male, because one autosome is smaller
The person has an extra pair of sex chromosomes
b.why: The 22 matching pairs are autosomes. A 23rd pair of different sizes is an X and a Y, which is a male. A female has two X chromosomes, which match in size.
b.clue: Which sex has a 23rd pair that does not match in size?

a.best: They carry the same genes, perhaps with different alleles

b.best: The person is male, with an X and a Y chromosome
